key_insight: High-pressure high-temperature synthesis significantly extends La doping in bilayer Sr3Ir2O7, enabling new magnetic and electronic states beyond ambient-pressure limits.
engineering_relevance: The work shows that synthesis route control can unlock otherwise inaccessible composition–property space, which is crucial for designing correlated oxide materials with tunable transport and magnetism.
method: Prepared nominal (Sr1-xLax)3Ir2O7 crystals with x = 0.05, 0.10, 0.15, and 0.20 using high-pressure high-temperature synthesis.
Verified composition and phase by single-crystal X-ray diffraction and SEM-EDX.
Compared structural, magnetic, and transport behavior across the doped series.
evidence_signal: X-ray refinement and SEM-EDX showed actual La contents exceeding nominal values, and the x = 0.20 sample no longer stabilized the bilayer phase but transformed to cubic perovskite Sr1-xLaxIrO3.
watch_item: The highest-doping sample loses the target bilayer phase, so phase stability becomes a key constraint when pushing La incorporation further.
paper_title: Extending the La Solubility Limit in Sr$_3$Ir$_2$O$_7$ through High-Pressure High-Temperature Synthesis
